headline: Commodity Markets Retreat on Hawkish Rate Bets and Cooling AI Rally
paragraphs: Precious metals and industrial commodities faced a bruising week, driven heavily by mounting Federal Reserve rate-hike bets that weighed across the board, alongside a cooling artificial intelligence rally that triggered copper's largest weekly drop since March. Silver tumbled 2.65 percent today and over 6 percent on the week, trapped in a descending channel as a stronger dollar and weaker jewellery purchases dented demand. Copper slid 1.92 percent on the day amid oversold conditions and the broader AI-driven market rout.

Gold managed a flat finish today at $3,887.60 per ounce, or EUR 3,518.12, but suffered a sharp 4.60 percent weekly loss—its biggest since June—while Goldman Sachs trimmed its year-end gold target to $4,150. Platinum fell 1.71 percent today, while palladium edged up 1.04 percent. The euro traded at 1.1050 against the dollar, amplifying European import costs slightly as local currency conversions sat around EUR 44.03 per ounce for silver and EUR 1,350.38 for platinum.

Crude oil posted back-to-back weekly losses, with Brent down over 2 percent for the week to $96.08 per bbl, pressured by a weaker demand outlook and news from the IEA that global oil supply has returned to surplus for the first time since the Iran war started. Natural gas dropped 2.93 percent today after a bigger-than-usual US storage build and fading weather demand, though it still finished the week up over 8 percent.
